Success-sector workspace cleanup is an independent promise, not implied by the doubly projected block; a one-qubit rotation supplies a concrete counterexample.

The inherited domain is0<x<1; the historical0<|x|<1 phrase is explicitly assessed, and the clean compression fixes U00 only. Rotation/reflection witnesses share U00=x and satisfy both Gram identities; they are distinct for s>0, with any negative-x extension explicitly outside the retained positive premise. Projected clean-basis action carries the same information as the clean block, not the full output vector; off-block completions and implementation resources are not uniquely determined.

The defined LCU stages have precise target/control registers and P† supplies the conjugate selector clean row. This architectural adjoint is sufficient, not uniquely forced by projected correctness; neither the clean block nor global unitarity implies deterministic auxiliary cleanup.

Derives the exact clean projected entry of the logical LCU matrix as a selector sum with SELECT matching indicator and conjugate-times-itself PREPARE weights, explaining the |prepare|^2 selection probability and the shared selector register.

For rational x,y embedded inR, both row norms are x²+y² and the cross overlap0, so D is orthogonal iff x²+y²=1. The question's real-completion existence has boundary|x|≤1, but rational witnesses need a rational square; universal clean-compression contraction rules out|c|>1 at normalizer1 in every auxiliary dimension.

The fixed-c reconstruction is equivalent to off-support zero entries; suitable c exists for every finite square one-sparse matrix, while a mismatched fixed c can fail and a two-nonzero column is not a counterexample to the existential premise. Zero columns and correctly located single nonzeros reconstruct exactly, including the empty square case; this entrywise identity does not supply unitary normalization or oracle/circuit resources.
Disjoint clean auxiliary registers compose blocks by matrix multiplication; X/X refutes naive same-register reuse, and neither reset nor inverse is a free coherent repair.

Shows the all-(-1) LCU filler phases give lower-right clean entry -N and so cannot equal S1 (whose lower-right block is 0) for nonzero normalizer, and gives the phase-balanced correction that recovers S1.

Permutation Gram sums give identity for a bijection, and finite-square injectivity already implies surjectivity; the historical alleged independent necessity is explicitly refuted. The injective product embedding yields a raw0/1 partial permutation in both rows and columns; a positive normalizer can rescale that block but supplies no arbitrary relative weights or circuit/resource certificate.
The three-bit source loader s |-> s XOR 3 is an involution with image list [3,2,1,0,7,6,5,4]; XOR-with-mask self-inversion is the circuit-level undoing of the two bit-flip gates.

Clean work guarantees the correct sum, unchanged row and return to zero. This concrete reversible circuit preserves row and entering work even on dirty inputs, whose arithmetic sum can—but need not—be wrong.

The reversible program gives E and the compiler emits a list plus exact stored phase; the inherited C remains the bare list product rather than full program denotation. P(E) is independently the0/1 basis-bijection matrix with rowE(c) in each column. Gate-case/list compiler soundness gives exp(i phi)C=P(E); the actual seven-wire witness has phi45pi/8 and bare C=exp(i3pi/8)P(E), refuting literal C=P(E). The corrected equality is a genuine phase-aware refinement between independent denotations, using chronological second-times-first composition. Full program denotation is exactly a permutation; bare C has the same support with a common nontrivial phase, so physical global-phase equivalence is not exact0/1 equality or a new cleanup/resource theorem.
A real planar rotation [[c,-s],[s,c]] over C is unitary exactly when c^2+s^2=1: the off-diagonals of the Gram matrix cancel identically and conjugation is trivial on real entries.

The inverse-cosine amplitude gate is unitary for every real parameter and for any extension of the angle, but its clean-entry readout equals the parameter only on [-1,1]; for |x|>1 the readout cannot equal x because cosine is bounded in [-1,1], proved without guessing the extension.

A block-diagonal operator built from per-block unitaries is unitary: the conjugate transpose respects the block structure, multiplication is pointwise in the control index, and each block collapses to the identity.

Same-bijection reindexing is a star-preserving algebra equivalence and preserves unitarity. Independent row/column bijections also preserve unitarity by two-sided unitary cancellation; what generally fails is using their fixed two-axis map as a unital multiplicative algebra equivalence.

Lifting a selector PREPARE to the full register as I ⊗ (PREPARE ⊗ I) preserves unitarity by applying the Kronecker-product-of-unitaries law twice; identities on untouched registers are inert unitaries.

A controlled SELECT (coeff,(s,x)) |-> (coeff,(s,p_s(x))) is a bijection with inverse applying (p_s)^{-1} under the same preserved selector s, hence unitary as a basis permutation; coherent control requires carrying the selector through for inversion.

Composition of basis-permutation matrices multiplies them in reverse order (second times first realizes first-then-second), because each column's single 1 collapses the product to function composition and left action forces the reversal.

The chosen PREPARE† SELECT AMPLITUDE PREPARE matrix is unitary by tensor/block/permutation, adjoint and product closure. Neither global unitarity nor a fixed clean projected block forces a unique final adjoint or deterministic auxiliary cleanup; full inverse uniqueness is a separate stronger requirement.

The ten named oracle-call labels fix exact printed order and length but are not interpreted matrices. No matrix, inverse/cleanup, unitarity or block-correctness assertion follows from the transcript or its length theorem. SWAP is a string label here; a separate executable object requires its own semantics/composition bridge. Visible backend total13 and effective projection10=declared9+visible padded0+trailing1 differ from the full internal-oracle pure-workspace budget6; an expanded physical footprint is not certified by these bookkeeping facts.

The indicator-oracle bundle certifies U is a permutation of a self-inverse label map, so U^2 = I and U-dagger = U; dagger-equals-itself plus self-inverse image make the same oracle its own exact clean uncompute, which permutation-ness alone (P-dagger = P^{-1} not P) would not guarantee.

exists_core_lq reshapes a core's (Fin 2 x Fin r) column index to a flat Fin (2r) index via a bijection, applies thin LQ, and reindexes back; A = R*Q and Q*Q-transpose = 1 hold with inner dimension min(l, 2r).
absorb A R contracts R into the right bond of A; absorb_slice shows slice(absorb A R, bit) = slice(A, bit) * R, so absorption is per-bit right multiplication that never mixes emitted-bit branches.

Evaluation interprets rational constants, assigned symbols, addition, multiplication and negation compositionally. It preserves these operations into Rat without identifying raw expression trees modulo ring laws.

A system-on-n-qubits candidate with a auxiliary qubits has a 2^(n+a) unitary; the signal register is high-order; the explicit product-register branch equals the flattened signal-system block projection.
Prescribed orthonormal columns placed at arbitrary distinct positions via an injection extend to an orthogonal matrix agreeing on those positions.
When r < N, prescribed orthonormal columns extend to a determinant-+1 orthogonal matrix by a single sign flip on an unused column, preserving all prescribed columns.
A(a|left>+b|right>) = a*col(left)+b*col(right) and row-k amplitude = a*A[k,left]+b*A[k,right], by linearity of mulVec on basis kets.
Projected-block pointwise equality to the target is equivalent to the clean-basis action equality, bridged by cleanBasisActionAmplitude = signalSystemBlockProjection entry.
Orthonormal columns (V-transpose V = I_r) force r <= N by independence; and when r < N an injective placement e : Fin r -> Fin N is non-surjective by card_le_of_surjective, leaving a spare position.

Zero-padding a right-canonical core preserves active clean-input column orthonormality (paddedCore_active_isometry) but destroys physical-register row orthonormality, since padded rows are zero (paddedCore_inactive_output).

The r < N hypothesis in exists_specialOrthogonal_completion is necessary: a fully-prescribed det=-1 orthonormal frame (e.g. diag(1,-1)) has no determinant-+1 completion, since no unused column remains for the sign-flip repair.
The backward recurrence new left bond = min(l, 2m') gives head_bound (l' <= l and l' <= 2m') and last_bond_le_two (penultimate bond <= 2 when the terminal bond is 1).

Wire renaming induces one specific permutation of bitstring labels. Each renamed primitive is conjugated by that permutation, so chronological products telescope; arbitrary unrelated basis permutations are not generally wire renamings.

A circuit uses only single-qubit rotations, bit flips and controlled bit flips. A bijection relabels all physical wires, preserving which wire controls which target. Which of total instruction count, rotation count and controlled-bit-flip count must stay unchanged? Does this alone prove equal nearest-neighbor routing cost on fixed hardware?

Define R(theta)=[[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]]. Derive the exact operator distance between R(a) and R(b), and prove it is at most |a-b|/2. Why does adding any number of untouched spectator qubits not multiply the distance by a dimension factor?

For the real rotation R(theta)=[[cos(theta/2),-sin(theta/2)],[sin(theta/2),cos(theta/2)]], compare R(theta+2pi) and R(theta). A colleague claims the two full operators have distance0 because every output probability agrees. Refute or prove that claim, and distinguish bare-system global-phase equivalence from coherent branch use.

A reversible gate flips a target bit exactly when two control bits are both1. Assume each control wire is distinct from the target, but allow the two control wires to coincide. Prove the gate is its own inverse and explain what it reduces to when the controls coincide.

On a two-bit string(c,t), consider the update that flips c itself when c=t=1 and otherwise does nothing. Does the familiar self-inverse proof for a two-control target flip remain valid when one control is also the target? Give a concrete collision and explain the lost hypothesis.

Let S and T be Hermitian matrices on one finite system and X a Hermitian matrix on a second system. Prove that H=S tensor X+T tensor I is Hermitian without assuming that S and T commute. Give a counterexample showing that the same conclusion can fail if X is not Hermitian.

A finite row stencil is a list of offset/coefficient pairs. Its matrix entry at row i and column j is the sum of coefficients of every pair with i+offset=j; no modular wrapping is used. Prove that merging repeated offsets by summing their coefficients leaves every matrix entry unchanged. Use the pairs (1,2),(1,-2),(-1,3) to show why list width and the number of nonzero matrix entries need not agree.
A half-angle plane rotation by the negative exact split angle sends a column pair (x,y) to (sqrt(x^2+y^2),0); the zero pair uses angle 0 and needs no division.
Mixing two rows by (a,b),(c,d) scales the determinant by a*d-b*c; for a plane rotation this factor is cos^2+sin^2=1, so the determinant is preserved.
Reversing a chronological list of plane rotations and negating every angle exactly inverts the sequence, by a single-step inverse law plus list induction.
A bottom-up adjacent sweep zeros a column strictly below its top window row while leaving rows outside the window untouched, by a zeroing induction protected by outside-invariance.
An orthonormal matrix with a column supported only on its diagonal has that pivot squaring to 1; a nonnegative-pivot guarantee pins it to exactly +1.
An orthogonal det-1 matrix whose first N-1 columns are the identity prefix must be the identity; the determinant hypothesis pins the final diagonal to +1 rather than a -1 reflection.
Consecutive binary-reflected Gray indices differ by exactly one physical wire flip, proved by width induction with parity-split head/tail casework.
The accumulated rotation transform is orthogonal with determinant 1, so its transpose times the upper-trapezoidal residual recovers the original rectangular matrix exactly.
Folding a left boundary vector into the first core of a matrix-product chain gives a scalar amplitude equal to the left-weighted sum of open-chain amplitudes, via a finite double-sum exchange.
Absorbing the right boundary vector into the last core of a matrix-product chain (terminal bond 1) reproduces the chronological matrix-vector readout at every incoming bond, by induction.
A matrix-product chain of n cores with bonds at most D stores at most 2*n*D^2 scalars; this is a stored-address count and not a bound on contraction arithmetic.

The strict upper-prefix invariant survives because the next sweep touches rows r>=k, all strictly below every earlier column c<k. No old diagonal entry is assumed zero; skipped pivots and empty dimensions are vacuous.

A greedy transposition process extending a finite injection agrees with the target injection on every original index, proved by a strengthened induction using injectivity to protect earlier placements.

Reorienting an orthogonal matrix to determinant 1 by a single sign-flip chosen from column-permutation parity yields an orthogonal det-1 matrix on both parity branches, without ever evaluating the determinant.
Symmetric Gray-coordinate relabeling of a matrix preserves orthogonality and the determinant exactly, because one shared row/column bijection makes it a multiplicative identity-fixing reindexing.

Reindexing an adjacent plane rotation by the Gray labeling equals a selected RY two-level plane on the Gray-flip wire; the half-angle is theta or -theta according to the first index's target bit, from the pair ordering.
Two basis states share a selected RY plane's control context if and only if they are equal or related by a single target-wire X, pinning the exact 2D pair the rotation can touch.

The unoptimized Gray/Givens producer emits L=N(N-1)/2 selected planes, each3*2^q-2 gates. Its exact family ratio G/N grows quadratically, while the N4 check only distinguishes stage cost from total cost; none is an optimal-synthesis lower bound.
Iterated step-by-step application of a plane-rotation list equals one multiplication by the accumulated matrix taken in reverse list order; the reverse order is forced by first-listed-acts-first.

In an eight-counter exact-real operation model, prove a stored two-row plane rotation on length-M rows costs exactly 6*M field, 10*M read and 6*M write operations, accounting for each from the three materialized passes.
Prove one stored rotation step costs 6*M field, 10*M+2*N+2 read and 6*M+2*N write operations, where the 2*N spine-copy term is a stipulated charge of the cost contract.
By induction on step count, prove a k-step column sweep is bounded by k*(step budget + emit) on every counter and emits exactly k records including zero-angle steps.
By list induction, prove a stored replay of L recorded rotations denotes the product of plane rotations (not formed densely) and costs L times a per-step budget plus one trailing read.

Prove the eight per-counter polynomial budgets of a stored rectangular compilation sum to N*M*(22*M+30*N+29)+5*N*N+4*N+M+1 and read it as an exact-real, not finite-bit, count. The write budget includes the required +2*N spine term.

A wide thin-LQ run has an exact sum of actual stage costs, but only an upper bound after the compiler cost is replaced by its polynomial budget; its deterministic factors satisfy the exact same-run LQ identities.
Prove a size-k monadic sum of equal-cost summands costs k*(B+one field), and specialize to a bond-D contraction entry costing D*(three reads + two field).
Prove the stored chain closure costs 20*D-squared+30*D+5*n-squared+7*n+constant, explaining the n-squared term as a reference-copy series and the n-independent left closure.
By chain induction, prove the stored Gram-environment computation costs at most n*(24*D-cubed+25*D-squared+20*D+6)+5*D-squared+4*D+6, with the cubic term from the per-node contractions.
Prove the stored tensor-train norm costs the Gram cost plus exactly two reads and one square root (total +3), and equals the Euclidean norm of the represented vector.
Prove the sum-over-tags total equals the eight-term enumerated total, is additive, zero on the zero cost and one on a unit charge, and explain why this enables compositional cost proofs.
Prove the four named integer counters of the stored Hermite raw-source run sum to 2*n-squared+10*n+7, and delineate the same-run scope excluding finite-bit runtime and normalization.
Prove a primitive circuit's parallel-scheduling depth is at most its gate count via the per-step inequality that one gate raises every wire depth by at most one.

Materialization has no uniform dimensions-only cost bound over unrestricted suppliers: a fixed one-by-one zero matrix can be supplied with arbitrarily many charged additions. Polynomial bounds require control of the supplier work, not merely a storage surcharge.

The angle budget is a componentwise upper bound. Zero inputs use no inverse cosine; nonzero inputs use one, but the full field budget is attained only when the negative-y sign branch executes its extra subtraction.
Boundary: the stored identity costs 5*N*N+4*N exact-real operations, nonzero for all N at least 1, free only at the degenerate N=0.
Counterexample: persistent log append costs the left length in reads and writes and is independent of the right length, so it is neither constant nor total-length dependent.
Boundary: the tall LQ branch (m>n) runs no sweep, returning the input plus an identity at cost one comparison + 5*n*n+4*n, refuting that thin-LQ always eliminates.

The actual positive-scale compiled injection flags encode the cutoff bits: right children never inject, and each left child injects exactly at a1 bit. Hence expCalls=n+2+popcount(cutoff), with sharp attainable range n+2..n+2+max(n,1); an explicit convention-aware migration is required.

One closed core has only unit scalar boundaries and actual maximum bond1 for everyD. With at least two cores the typed internalD bonds remain, giving actual max(D,1); this structural fact is separate from minimal tensor rank and construction cost.

Probability mixtures are density states and pure states are precisely their extreme points. Relative boundary in the trace-one Hermitian affine space means singular density states, whereas the full Hermitian/complex ambient boundary is every density state; the original unrestricted boundary=pure request is false.

Column isometries preserve the ensemble outer-product sum, but zero rows and phase redundancies must be handled. Explicit rotation of two positive spectral components gives genuinely varying ensembles for every mixed state, and a rectangular isometry can give a genuinely longer positive ensemble.

Product states give independent local outcomes, but separable mixtures can be classically correlated; purity forces a separable state to be a single uncorrelated product, so correlated separable states are necessarily mixed.

The two-qubit Werner state is entangled exactly for negative swap overlap. Its partial transpose has eigenvalue x/2, while the separable converse follows by twirling an explicit product state with overlap x and identifying the unique Werner state, not by reversing swap-overlap positivity.

Entrywise checks certify an exact unit-factor block encoding and equal the operator identity, but approximate embedding is defined by an operator-norm bound that small per-entry errors can violate after dimensional accumulation.

SVD gives an exact one-ancilla unitary dilation of every contraction. Its chosen branch has probability||A b||^2, but exact-operator nonunitarity does not force probabilistic normalized state preparation: cI has the identity as its normalized target procedure.
A homomorphism automatically preserves the identity and inverses, which is exactly why a representation phi satisfies phi(e)=1_V and phi(g^{-1})=phi(g)^{-1} with invertibility free.
Averaging an arbitrary inner product over a finite group yields a G-invariant inner product making the representation unitary, so orthogonal complements of invariant subspaces are invariant.
Averaging a projection over the group produces an equivariant projection onto the invariant subspace whose kernel is an invariant complement, provided |G| is invertible in the field.

Functional equivariance does not imply linearity, even for entire maps on finite unitary irreps. Once common-field linearity is an explicit conditional premise, invariant kernel/image subspaces yield zero-or-linear-isomorphism; scalar Schur additionally needs an eigenvalue route.

Functional equivariance is insufficient even for entire maps on finite unitary irreps. For explicitly linear endomorphisms, positive finite dimension and algebraic closure supply an eigenvalue; the shifted linear Schur lemma then gives the scalar commutant, with zero-space and exterior-field/dimension limits explicit.

The unrestricted algebraic abelian-irrep claim fails on C(t). In nonzero finite complex dimension, commuting action operators are scalar by eigenvalue-based Schur, so an invariant line is the whole irrep; real and zero/infinite-dimensional boundaries remain explicit.
Pauli conjugation permutes operator-conjugation terms modulo phases only when the right adjoint is retained; Schur and trace then give the maximally mixed output on C^2.

A finite-dimensional trace character is a conjugacy-invariant K-valued function with chi(e)=(dim_K V)*1_K. Integer degree is uniquely recovered in characteristic zero, but generally only its residue is visible in positive characteristic.
Character orthonormality turns multiplicities into inner products n_i = (chi_i, chi_V), from which irreducibility (norm-squared one) and the isomorphism-iff-equal-characters criterion follow.
The multiplicity of an irreducible U in V equals dim Hom_G(U, V): additivity splits the intertwiner space, Schur makes self-intertwiners one-dimensional and cross-intertwiners zero.

Group-averaging an operator produces an equivariant operator that, on a multiplicity-free decomposition into two inequivalent irreps, is block diagonal with scalar diagonal blocks (Schur ii) and vanishing off-diagonal blocks (Schur i).

The flip is a commuting involution over any field. Characteristic different from2 gives complementary algebraic eigenspace projectors; orthogonal projections require the specified real/complex tensor-product metric, not merely involutivity. Characteristic2 and incompatible metrics expose the old scope gap.

Averaging the representation over G gives the orthogonal projection onto the invariant vectors V^G, whose trace counts the trivial-representation multiplicity, the trivial case of the character projection formula.

When an isotypical component has multiplicity greater than one, the symmetrized operator's diagonal block is identity-on-irrep tensor an arbitrary multiplicity-space operator, so it need not be a scalar - a concrete S_2 swap counterexample.

The invariant image of I-swap gives a proper nonzero tensor-square subspace over every field and algebraic dimension>=2. Finite symmetric/alternating counts specialize to the source's complex +/- decomposition; characteristic2 and infinite cardinal counts need explicit distinctions. A one-dimensional square has character chi^2, not generally chi.

Isotypical components are unique but splitting a multiplicity-greater-than-one component into individual irreducible subspaces is not, as shown by two distinct trivial-line splittings of the symmetric subspace of (C^2)^{(x)2}.
Implementing a POVM through shared-beta block encodings of sqrt(P_i) gives postselection success probability exactly 1/(beta^2 2^m), with completeness collapsing the state-dependent sum.
After postselection the POVM circuit yields outcome i with probability <psi|P_i|psi> and the correct sqrt(P_i)-update, with the mixed-state rule following by linearity.
Correct complex conjugation fixes the forced-weight contradiction for conclusive-only unambiguous discrimination; the positive inconclusive effect provides the slack for a valid three-outcome POVM.
The two-conclusive-one-inconclusive discrimination POVM is valid: P_? = I - P_psi - P_phi stays PSD because P_psi+P_phi has operator norm exactly 1.

POVM selector correctness depends on one specified clean projector and normalized coefficient weights, not shared physical ancillas. A union-zero projection works for clean disjoint branches; beta compensation uses the Euclidean norm of the factors.

Compute-rotate-uncompute gives an exact coherent oracle for the stored-angle cosine. Discarding the angle record dephases joint signal/index classes, not the signal marginal; basis inputs and equal records are exceptions to a blanket decoherence claim.

An entry-derived amplitude oracle needs original queries plus reversible arithmetic, signed/complex signal loading and cleanup. A fused O;C;R;C†;O† implementation uses one forward and inverse ENTRY query while charging both arithmetic passes and all live workspace; two derived-angle calls are a different ledger.

A diagonal entry-amplitude oracle gives a unit-scale block; for nonzero A the sharp existence scale is ||A||, whereas A=0 admits all positive scales with unattained infimum0. No efficient synthesis inferred.

A Hermitian clean block does not force a Hermitian unitary completion. Definition9.23 adds global self-adjointness; the exact scaled qubitization proof is Eq10.30-10.40, with2D interior sectors and1D endpoint sectors.

The induced block A~ = ((Xi')_{N'})^dagger U_A Xi_N has entries <psi_i|U_A|phi_j> and equals the compression Pi' U_A Pi in the chosen bases; ||A - alpha A~|| <= eps generalizes the computational-basis definition.

For a Hermitian block encoding, each eigenvector is qubitized into a 2D subspace where U_A is a reflection and O = U_A Z_Pi a rotation; O^k has top-left T_k(lambda_i), so (U_A Z_Pi)^k block-encodes the Chebyshev polynomial T_k(A).
The commutant of End(V) tensor 1 inside End(V tensor W) is exactly 1 tensor End(W), proved by a block-matrix argument.
For an isotypical representation the commutant is the sum of multiplicity-space endomorphism algebras and the double commutant recovers A.

The permutation algebra and the algebra spanned by the common GL(V) action g^tensor(n) are mutual commutants. Pure-tensor commutation and interpolation from invertible shifts prove the GL claim without a unitary-only span substitution.
The symmetric subspace of a tensor power is spanned by the n-fold powers of single vectors, proved by polarization and a closedness argument.

With the source convention e_T=r_T*c_T, columns act first. More than d rows force signed column cancellation on every basis word, hence c_T=0 on the whole tensor space and the Young-image piece is absent, without commuting row and column sums.
The antisymmetrizer on the n-fold tensor power of C^d is identically zero when n exceeds d, since no wedge of n distinct basis vectors exists.
Explicit Schur-Weyl dimension count for the fourth power of C^3 verifying eighty-one equals the sum of products of the two piece dimensions over the four admissible diagrams.
The two-dimensional unitary irreducible piece for a two-part partition has dimension lambda_1 minus lambda_2 plus one, from both tableau counting and the determinant-times-symmetric-power form.
The hook length formula gives thirty-five standard tableaux for shape (4,2,1) and exactly one for a single row or single column of n boxes.
Permutations are conjugate exactly when they share a cycle type, proved via the identity that conjugation relabels cycle entries by the conjugating permutation.
Twirling sends any state to a twirl-invariant Werner state whose visibility, measured against the swap, equals that of the original state.
Permutation-invariant operators on the tensor power of a fixed-dimension system are determined by only polynomially many parameters, via Schur-Weyl blocks and polynomial dimension bounds.

Schur-Weyl block probabilities have relative-entropy exponential rate with explicit polynomial prefactors; summing over diagrams proves total concentration in fixed neighborhoods of the spectrum, not exact matching or constant atom weights.

Partial transpose transports isotropic and Werner OPERATOR symmetries involutively, but may destroy positivity: Phi_d maps to F/d. The state-level equivalence holds exactly for the isotropic PPT case, not for all isotropic states.

The isotropic family has trace1 for all real x. At d>=2 positivity holds exactly on[0,d^2/(d^2-1)] with tight spectral endpoints; at d=1 the whole family equals I for every real x because the complementary sector is absent.
Exact extendibility thresholds with Werner fraction(1-d)/k; all d>=3 states2extendible, finite isotropic k cutoff and allk parameter limits.

The converse of channel-preserved extendibility fails: the depolarizing channel sends the non-2-extendible Phi+ to a 2-extendible isotropic state, so a channel can create extendibility the input lacked.

The mixed bound uses the chosen symmetric purification's d^2-dimensional local pairs and partial-trace contraction. Both displayed bounds vanish for k=o(n) at fixed d; at fixed accuracy the exact unrounded factor d compares excess n-k, not total n or rounded integer minima.
A single cloning unitary can serve a pair only if the states are orthogonal or equal, since unitarity forces the overlap to satisfy z = z^2; e.g. |0> and |+> cannot be cloned.
The optimal cloner's fidelity d_N/d_M exceeds 1 - Kd/N (tending to 1 for fixed K), and because it is input-independent its worst-case and Haar-average fidelities coincide, making it optimal for both.

The partition estimator lambda/n is always a valid ordered spectrum, but exact equality need not ever occur for irrational r. The polynomial-qualified KL bound plus the explicit diagram count proves fixed-epsilon convergence in probability, with zero-spectrum support handled separately.

Separable states are infinitely extendible via index-shared copies on each B_j, and k-extendibility descends to all k' <= k by discarding systems, yielding the monogamy inclusion chain Ext_1 superset ... superset SEP.

A purification Schmidt-decomposed across (AB : B'C) whose AB-marginal is the rank-one psi_AB must collapse to a single term, forcing rho_{A B B'} = psi_AB tensor omega_{B'} and ruling out 2-extensions of pure entangled states.
Applying the channel independently to each B_i of a k-extension yields a k-extension of (id tensor N)(rho_AB); CP gives positivity and TP gives both unit trace and the marginal-reduction identity.
Transpose trick and exact U tensor bar U invariance in a fixed basis, with explicit counterexample and source discrepancy for un-conjugated U tensor U.
Averaging |phi><phi|^{tensor n} over Haar pure states gives, by irreducibility of U^{tensor n} on Sym^n and Schur's lemma, exactly (1/d_sym) Pi_sym, with the constant fixed by the trace.

The symmetric-projection cloner has input-independent fidelity d_N/d_M for every pure state, because phi^{tensor M} is Pi_M-invariant and |phi><phi| is an idempotent of unit trace, so it saturates the optimal-cloning bound.

Compact normalized left Haar supplies right invariance for W=UV and hence channel covariance. Schur's scalar conclusion applies to the symmetric compression of an invariant-input output, not arbitrary outputs or the channel as a whole.

Permutation twirling preserves each product-state distribution; unitary twirling instead averages risks over a unitary orbit and preserves uniform spectrum guarantees. Both symmetries force block scalars, hence weak Schur measurement plus classical postprocessing.

Because the symmetric projector absorbs permutations (Pi_n Q_pi = Pi_n), the symmetrization average collapses and Pi_n rhobar Pi_n = Pi_n rho Pi_n, so symmetric-subspace compression cannot distinguish a state from its symmetrization.
Symmetric cloning map complete positivity via multi-Kraus identity extension and exact trace pairing; trace preserved on all symmetric support, not only separable pure-power mixtures.
The de Finetti fidelity ratio factorizes into d-1 increasing terms, so replacing them by the smallest, applying Bernoulli, and a crude comparison yields the clean lower bound 1 - kd/m.

Occupation orbits give the exact symmetric dimension and polynomial/exponential gap. Those facts do not put invariant mixed states in the original symmetric subspace: mixed de Finetti uses paired symmetric purification, while a projected cloning core and its full-channel completion have different support/trace domains.

Exact Hermitian clean blocks admit guaranteed adjoint-paired Chebyshev transformations: E^k gives T_{2k}(A) and UR E^k gives T_{2k+1}(A) after projection. U and U† have directed between-plane maps; neither distinct planes nor failure of every special unpaired construction follows from U≠U†.

Powering the plane rotation produces first-kind Chebyshev on the diagonal and second-kind Chebyshev times sqrt(1-t^2) off-diagonal; the prefactor forces the off-diagonal to vanish at the spectral endpoints.

selected_question_rubrics.question: A POVM P = {P_i : i in [2^m]} is implemented through block encodings as follows. For each outcome i we are given a unitary U_i that is a (beta, a)-block-encoding of sqrt(P_i), all sharing the SAME ancilla size a and the SAME subnormalization factor beta > 0, so that U_i |0^a> |psi> = (1/beta) |0^a> sqrt(P_i) |psi> + |perp_i>, where (<0^a| tensor I)|perp_i> = 0. selected_question_rubrics.question: Let U_A in HBE_{1,m}(A) be a Hermitian block encoding of a Hermitian A with ||A|| <= 1, spectral decomposition A = sum_i lambda_i |v_i><v_i|, so that U_A |0^m>|v_i> = lambda_i |0^m>|v_i> + sqrt(1-lambda_i^2)|perp_i> with Pi|perp_i> = 0, Pi = |0^m><0^m| tensor I. selected_question_rubrics.question: Work in an exact-real word-operation model that keeps eight separate running counters: field operations, square roots, inverse-cosine calls, other trigonometric calls, exact comparisons, stored-word reads, stored-word writes, and emitted records. A plane rotation acts on two stored length-M real rows u and v with coefficients c and s, returning rows whose j-th entries are c*u_j - s*v_j and s*u_j + c*v_j. Every materialized pass over M indices additionally charges two reads and two writes per index to write each intermediate value and read it back for projection, and each single entry-pair is computed with exactly the six field operations c*u_j, s*v_j, s*u_j, c*v_j, their difference, and their sum. Eight independent primitive counters; each primitive call costs one unit of its own counter

Original derivation from inspected local source; no fresh Lean verification

Correctly charge the two-read/two-write materialization surcharge on all three passes
Derive the exact totals 6*M field, 10*M read, 6*M write with per-pass accounting

selected_question_rubrics.question: In the eight-counter exact-real model, a column sweep eliminates entries below a pivot by performing a chronological chain of elimination steps. The per-step budget is independent of the angle-computation branch

Prove the k*(B+emit) upper bound using the branch-independent step budget
Prove the emit counter equals exactly k including zero-angle steps, distinguishing exact count from upper bound

selected_question_rubrics.question: A rectangular elimination records a chronological list of two-row rotation steps. assumptions: Recorded steps carry an exact angle and a pair of adjacent rows
Eight independent primitive counters in the exact-real model
conventions: The accumulated transform is replayed, never formed as a dense matrix product; costs are not finite-bit runtimes
Original derivation from inspected local source; no fresh Lean verification

Identify the per-step budget: one field, two trig, one rotation, and three reads
Derive total cost L*budget + one read with the trailing read from the empty-list base case

selected_question_rubrics.question: Consider a bivariate real array F(x,y) = q(u(x) + v(y)), where q is a real polynomial of degree at most d and u, v are arbitrary real-valued functions of the row index x and column index y respectively. selected_question_rubrics.question: On the invariant plane attached to a value t in the closed interval from minus one to one, the qubitization iterate acts as the plane rotation M = [[t, -sqrt(1-t^2)],[sqrt(1-t^2), t]]. selected_question_rubrics.question: In the cosine-sine view of qubitization the flag reflection is built from the single-qubit operator Z acting on the ancilla flag, and the large outer unitaries that diagonalize the construction are block-diagonal with respect to the split between the flag sector and its orthogonal complement. selected_question_rubrics.question: To build a block encoding of a linear combination of even Chebyshev transforms, sum over k from 0 to K-1 of coefficients times the degree-2k Chebyshev transform, one needs a select operation that, conditioned on an index register holding k, applies the degree-2k transform. selected_question_rubrics.question: Suppose an operator A maps an N-dimensional input space into an N'-dimensional output space and is accessed through a single unitary U on a larger space together with two projectors: an input projector of rank N and an output projector of rank N'. selected_question_rubrics.question: Take the smallest nontrivial subspace-encoding example: a four-dimensional space, the identity as the accessing unitary, an input projector that keeps the first qubit in its zero state, and an output projector obtained by rotating the input projector by a real angle theta on the first qubit (via the planar rotation with cosine theta on the diagonal and the usual off-diagonal signs). selected_question_rubrics.question: View Grover's single-marked search through qubitization beyond the computational basis. selected_question_rubrics.question: Call a bipartite state rho_AB k-extendible if there is a state rho_{A B_1 ... B_k} on A and k copies of B whose marginal on A B_i equals rho_AB for every i. selected_question_rubrics.question: Let V be a finite-dimensional complex vector space and let the symmetric subspace of its n-fold tensor power be the set of tensors fixed by every permutation of the n factors. selected_question_rubrics.question: Two permutations in the symmetric group are conjugate if and only if they have the same cycle type. selected_question_rubrics.question: A permutation-invariant operator on the n-fold tensor power of C^d, meaning one unchanged by conjugation by every factor permutation, is determined by only polynomially many parameters in n when d is held fixed. selected_question_rubrics.question: For the logical unprepare-select-amplitude-prepare LCU matrix on registers coefficient x (selector x system), derive the exact clean projected entry between clean input (clean coefficient, clean selector, systemColumn) and clean output (clean coefficient, clean selector, systemRow). selected_question_rubrics.question: In an LCU-style assembly of a Hermitian piece, each selected term contributes a scaled controlled-phase source whose upper block carries the intended operator and whose lower-right filler block is normalizer times a phase e^{i*phi}.
